ASCO-OFDM uses asymmetric clipping for odd subcarriers and symmetric clipping for even subcarriers.
E-ASCO-OFDM uses 3N/4 subcarriers for data transmission, where N is the FFT size.
The spectral efficiency of ASCO-OFDM is 37.5% compared to conventional OFDM.
The proposed PE-ASCO-OFDM system introduces precoding techniques to reduce PAPR.
Precoding techniques used include DHT, DCT, DST, and VLM.
DHT achieves 1.35 dB PAPR reduction.
DCT achieves 1.46 dB PAPR reduction.
DST achieves 2.12 dB PAPR reduction.
VLM achieves 2.17 dB PAPR reduction.
PAPR is defined as the ratio of maximum instantaneous power to average power.
Hermitian symmetry is applied to ensure real-valued signals for VLC.
The PE-ASCO-OFDM system maintains the same data rate and BER performance as conventional E-ASCO-OFDM.
High PAPR can cause LED-induced nonlinear distortions.
Precoding approaches do not require side information transmission.
The CCDF is used to evaluate PAPR reduction techniques.
ASCO-OFDM has higher data rates than ACO-OFDM and FLIP-OFDM.
ASCO-OFDM maintains acceptable BER performance compared to DCO-OFDM.
LACO-OFDM with two layers matches the data rate of ASCO-OFDM.
Increasing layers in LACO-OFDM increases the data rate.
The arrangement of data symbols helps recover clipped parts at the receiver.
The PE-ASCO-OFDM system improves power efficiency and spectral efficiency.
The paper provides a comprehensive performance analysis of PE-ASCO-OFDM in terms of PAPR and BER.
The analytical expression for PAPR and simulation results are explained and analyzed.
The proposed techniques are invertible, allowing signal recovery at the receiver.
The main challenge is balancing high data rate and good BER performance in VLC systems.
